question.:question/worked-solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A) & =\begin{vmatrix}\sqrt{13} & 4 \\ 5 & 5\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\cdot 5-4\cdot 5 \\  & =5\sqrt{13}-20 \\  & =-20+5\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Calculate $det(Z)$, if
$Z=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{x} & {y}^{5} \\ y & \sqrt{x}\end{bmatrix}$
Assume $x\geq 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(Z) & =\begin{vmatrix}\sqrt{x} & {y}^{5} \\ y & \sqrt{x}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot \sqrt{x}-{y}^{5}\cdot y \\  & =x-{y}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$
